messages.subject: Observer configuration on IO platforms
parts:
I am switching from a "trial" configuration to a full double platform ("Independent Observer) configuration in an aerial survey, with two observers (one on each side) on each of two platforms.

Is there any advantage or disadvantage to rotating observers between sides within platforms? Or even between platforms? 

My expectation is that there might be a variance penalty to rotation, as different observers would be paired up in the sight-resight data. Also, it may be that some observers might have a "good" side and a "bad" side, in terms of their observing performance. 

On the other hand, some observers like to switch sides at least every day, as this lets them use a different body position to avoid "repetitive strain" type problems. So, other things being equal, it would be nice to be able to switch.

Any advice welcome,

Daniel Pike.



Not rotating observers should decrease variance?

does 1x2 + 3x4 choose increase variance?
